parsedVerdict.reasoning: The class sits in the domain layer. Its main job is a business rule that fits there: it computes the share of the portfolio held in emerging markets, checks it against the min and max thresholds, and supplies default thresholds (0.08 and 0.12) in getSettings. But the same class also does presentation work. evaluate() and getName() turn the result into localized text for the user by calling the injected I18nService with message ids and placeholders. evaluate() also formats numbers for display: values are multiplied by 100 and passed through toPrecision(3) to make percentage strings. getConfiguration() returns settings for a UI control (step 0.01, unit '%', and flags for showing threshold inputs). Rendering text and configuring widgets are presentation concerns. The domain rule should return the raw result (true/false, the ratio and the thresholds) and leave translation, number formatting and widget setup to the presentation layer. This mix is a design pattern the codebase uses throughout, not a one-off. That is why confidence is moderate.
